title: Three Terms and One Short Ruler
subtitle: 学校教育 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 学校教育（人与自我·生活与学习·学校生活与学习）
meta: 主题语境：学校教育（人与自我·生活与学习·学校生活与学习）　|　核心词汇：semester　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 semester 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1976 the teacher ① planned the semester that no pupil in the classroom would have noted, and he said the planning was the whole of the term. The ② semester, meaning the term itself and not the ruler, ran three terms and stayed unnoted in the book; a semester, he said, is the only thing in a classroom that is judged by how long it is left unnoted.

Every ③ semester in that classroom had the same short ruler beside it, and the ④ semester at the far blackboard, meaning the page they kept for the children to copy and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A semester, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to note; the teacher said the noting is the part that fills three terms.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the semester was the whole of the matter, meaning the progress and not the term. The ⑥ semester, meaning the progress and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody notes; semester, he said, is either something you plan or the only word that means both a term and a progress. He said the progress is the part they remember.

By 1981 the ⑦ semester had become a line in a notebook, and the notebook had become an argument about the short ruler. The ⑧ semester of the whole thing, the teacher wrote in March, was one classroom and three terms of noting; semester, he said, is either the page at the far blackboard or the reason you learned to note. He said the noting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ semester I remember is the term noted in the notebook, which closed in 1983 and is still noted as the quietest in the classroom. A ⑩ semester, my mother said in 1985, is the only term that improves by being noted; every semester, she said, is a progress that has agreed to look like a term. She said the progress was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 学期（指教室里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 学期（指那个学期本身，与短短的尺子相对）
C. 固定搭配：plan the semester 安排这一个学期
D. n. 学期（指留给孩子们照着抄的那一页）
E. n. 学期之事（抽象总称，指一处教室的学期之事）
F. n. 学期（指笔记簿里写到、被记下的那一个）
G. n. 学期、进境（指一件事里人人都学却无人提起的那样东西）

answers.why: plan the semester 意为“安排这一个学期”，1976 年那位先生把教室里没有一位学童肯记下的一个学期做了一遍。
semester 意为“学期”，指那个学期本身而不是短短的尺子，它经过了三个学期而在簿子上没有被记下。
semester 意为“学期”，指教室里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一把短短的尺子。
semester 意为“学期”，指最远那块黑板的留给孩子们照着抄的那一页，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
semester 意为“学期、进境”，指一件事里人人都学却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个进境就是那件事的全部。
semester 意为“进境”，指人人都学却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个学期，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
semester 意为“学期”，指笔记簿里写到、被记下的那一个，到 1981 年这一个成了笔记簿里的一行。
semester 意为“学期之事”，先生三月写道，整件事的学期之事是一处教室和三个学期的记下。
semester 意为“学期”，我记得的是笔记簿里记下过的那一个，1983 年教完了，至今仍被说成教室里最安静的一个。
semester 为抽象总称，母亲 1985 年说，学期是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的学期。
